_about: The narrated cut's timeline, written by narrate.py from narration.json: each scene lasts its lead-in, its clip and its air; captions (`cues`) are the scene text cut at sentences and long clauses, timed by letter count and snapped to the voice's pauses; a scene that waits on its read carries `pending` and plays its picture silent, at the film's own pace. Each scene's `anchors`, added by cues.py, pin a reveal (`at`, film seconds into the scene) to the narration time `t` of the word that names it (`said` is that word's onset; `t` differs only where the picture needs the room). build.py narrated reads it; do not edit by hand.

layout._why: The funding film's narrated pacing: each scene is its lead-in (the seam, its barrier and the first reveal), its clip, and its air.

cues.text: Greetings, Noncredit CPL Heroes!
It's a great day for our system as we continue to build out our shared CPL tools to serve noncredit learners.
Special thanks to our legislative partners,
who supported the Board of Governors' and Chancellor Christian's request for an additional thirty-five million dollars in CPL funding.
Here's how noncredit learning becomes college credit.
Last year,
Chancellor Christian said that noncredit and not-for-credit learners would be key to our CPL goal.
Our colleges have served more than fifty-two thousand students through CPL so far.
By twenty thirty,
CPL for about seventy-five hundred noncredit learners a year is within reach.
About one in four of our students takes a noncredit course each year.
More than thirty thousand students earned a noncredit award in twenty twenty-four to twenty-five.
And noncredit students who were working before they enrolled saw their median quarterly wages rise thirty-four percent a year after finishing or leaving their program.
Mira's free noncredit community health worker courses at Cabrillo College mirror credit courses.
She earned eight units of credit and a Certificate of Achievement without retaking a class.
Emilio earned his EMT certification through Moreno Valley College's noncredit program.
The college awards eight and a half units for it,
toward a paramedic or fire technology degree and on to a bachelor's in emergency management.
Carla climbed Mount San Antonio College's noncredit health ladder to the LVN license.
College of the Desert awards twenty-two units for that license toward an associate degree in nursing,
and Mount San Antonio College plans to document its own ladder.
Nadia is finishing a noncredit IT support certificate at North Orange Continuing Education.
She holds three CompTIA certifications, A plus, Network plus and Security plus.
Twelve colleges award credit for all three,
and at Saddleback College they carry nine units toward an associate degree in information technology.
Faculty have already said yes.
At twenty-eight colleges,
seventy-eight percent of eligible EMT units reach a transcript,
and forty-nine statewide credit determinations sit ready at two hundred fifty-three college sites.
Most of the opportunity is still ahead.
Now, something to celebrate!
The state budget provides thirty-five million dollars one-time and seven million ongoing for CPL.
Last year, fifty-thousand-dollar grants went to four noncredit programs.
This year,
one point eight million dollars in noncredit funding reaches every community college noncredit program.
Credit and noncredit FTES together size every max award.
Three invitations to the field.
Mirror a course.
Post your certificates in MAP.
Invite your completers back.
The CPL Initiative team will help you with each one.
Our time is now!
